name: Basalt-Throne
description: Basalt-Throne is a colossal gas giant so dark it appears almost solid, its atmosphere layered in shades of charcoal, slate, and volcanic black that give it the appearance of a world carved from basalt. A thin debris ring of captured asteroids and destroyed moons encircles the equator, glinting faintly against the planet's brooding darkness. The magnetic field is extraordinarily powerful, generating radiation belts that extend millions of kilometers into surrounding space.

Approaching Basalt-Throne feels like descending into a gravity well with teeth. The planet's mass warps local spacetime enough to affect navigational calculations, and the radiation belts demand heavy shielding. The storms in the upper atmosphere are invisible from a distance, their darkness indistinguishable from the clouds around them, but they move at speeds that would shred any vessel caught within.

The debris ring contains the remains of at least nine spacecraft that miscalculated their approach, their wreckage now permanently captured in orbit alongside natural fragments. The planet has no moons, likely having consumed or ejected them over its lifetime, and the gravitational perturbations in its vicinity suggest an anomalous mass distribution within the core. Some theorists propose a collapsed stellar remnant at its center, though this remains unconfirmed.

Basalt-Throne's fuel reserves are immense but harvesting operations must contend with the crushing gravity, lethal radiation, and unpredictable gravitational fluctuations near the planet. The satellite graveyard in the debris ring is itself a salvage opportunity, though navigating the ring safely requires exceptional piloting. The dark giant sits at the center of its system like a sovereign on a throne of stone, demanding tribute from any who approach.
